title: I SAW, I COVETED, I TOOK

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Achan replied, "It is true! I have sinned against the Lord, the God of Israel. This is what I have done: When I saw in the plunder a beautiful robe from Babylonia, two hundred shekels of silver and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels, I coveted them and took them. They are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath." — Josh 7:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At last Achan confesses, and his own words trace the anatomy of sin with painful clarity: "I saw... I coveted... I took... I hid." This is the age-old pattern, the very steps that first led humanity astray. Eve "saw that the fruit was good... and took some and ate it" (Gen 3:6). It is the same sequence that trapped David with Bathsheba. Sin usually begins not with a dramatic leap but with a lingering look.

Notice the progression. First, Achan saw the forbidden things — a look is not yet sin. But then he let the look become longing: "I coveted them." He fed the desire instead of turning away. Coveting led to grasping — "I took them" — and grasping led to concealing — they are "hidden in the ground inside my tent." Every step made the next one easier. Sin is a slippery slope that gathers speed.

The lesson is to break the chain early. Had Achan turned his eyes away at the first glance, none of this would have followed. We cannot always stop the first look, but we can refuse to let it become a lingering gaze of desire. As Scripture warns, desire, once conceived, "gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death" (Jas 1:15).

The good news of the gospel is that Christ breaks this chain at its root. He forgives what we have done and, by His Spirit, gives us power to turn away at the first look, to say no to covetous desire, and to walk in freedom. We need not be enslaved to the old pattern of see, covet, take, hide.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where in your life does sin tend to begin with a "lingering look"?
2. At which point in the chain — seeing, coveting, taking, hiding — could you break free earlier?
3. How does Christ give you power to turn away before desire becomes sin?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me break the chain of sin at the first look. Guard my eyes and my desires, and give me power through Your Spirit to turn away and walk in freedom. Amen.
